forecaster_note: Wed 9 Sep — "Looking at a window of quality surf through the morning. Then building onshore and lumpy." Wind should hold off in the morning for clean head-high-plus surf at the south exposures and fun sized stuff elsewhere for those that want to cruise. Then another south wind switch moves through about 10/11am with onshore, lumpy and building surf for the rest of the day. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: Light WSW offshore at dawn Wed — swings S and onshore around 10–11am.

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Day's over. Short S swell peaked hard — 1057 kJ at 100% consistency — but only the dawn SW offshore hour was worth it. Long Reef held 8–10ft of wind-affected lump all day.

dee-why.window: Gone. Dawn–8am had the SW offshore before it went cross-shore S and lumped up.
alerts: Dead S swell at 174° — wrapped badly into the bay, as it always does

tip.label: Frontside — Dee Why Point
tip.text: 1057 kJ is a big number but at 9 seconds it's all push and no shape. The Point was the only place holding a wall today.

long-reef.window: Too much water moving with S onshore on it all day.

curl-curl.window: Onshore from 9am. Not worth the paddle.

manly.window: Smallest and most sheltered — the least bad option, which isn't saying much.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: One clean window: dawn to ~9am on light WSW offshore. Long Reef and Curl Curl carry the size at 4–6ft; Dee Why is smaller and the SSE 159° swell wraps poorly. S wind switch ~10–11am then it builds to 8–12ft of onshore mess by dark.

dee-why.window: Dawn–9am only. Your usual 10–12 slot lands on the wrong side of the wind switch tomorrow.
alerts: S wind switch 10–11am — rating falls off a cliff after that
Swell direction SSE 159° wraps badly into Dee Why

long-reef.window: Pick of the four, dawn–9am. Best size with the offshore still on it.
alerts: Builds to 8–12ft and blows out by evening

curl-curl.window: Solid early option if Long Reef is crowded. Same dawn–9am rule.

manly.window: Small but holds clean the longest — the fallback if you can't get out before 9am.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat 12 is the pick — SSE swell fading to a workable 4–6ft with W/NW offshore until the NE seabreeze fills around midday. Sun 13 halves to 2–3ft but stays clean, sunny and offshore early. Energy eases 167 kJ Sat to 97 kJ Sun. Your 10–12 window works both days.

dee-why.window: Sat: 4–5ft, offshore W/NW till ~11am — best Dee Why has looked all week. Sun: 2–3ft and clean early.
alerts: NE seabreeze from midday both days

long-reef.window: Sat holds the most size at 5–7ft. Sun settles to a mellow 3–4ft.

curl-curl.window: Sat 4–6ft with the early offshore. Sun drops to a fun 3–4ft.

manly.window: Small both days. Only worth it if you want an easy longboard cruise.
